_note: The Story of Prophet Idris (Enoch), drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs Maryam, al-Anbiya). The Qur'an honours him with two brief passages — a man of truth and a prophet, patient and righteous, raised to a high station — and relates no extended narrative; this chronicle says only what the text says. He stands between Adam and Nuh. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: A Man of Truth and a Prophet
events.summary: 'And mention in the Book Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.' The Qur'an names him among those it commands the Prophet to remember, and grants him the two highest honours of speech and standing — truthfulness (ṣiddīq) and prophethood.
events.why: Before any deed is told, the Qur'an fixes Idris's character in a single word — ṣiddīq, utterly truthful — the foundation on which prophethood is built, and the reason his name is worth remembering.

events.title: Raised to a High Station
events.summary: 'And We raised him to a high station.' In a single verse the Qur'an records Idris's honour before Allah — an elevation of rank and nearness granted to a truthful prophet, without the text detailing its manner.
events.why: The Qur'an lets the honour stand without embellishment: a righteous servant is lifted to a high place with his Lord. Where the text is brief, the believer's knowledge stays brief and content.

events.title: Among the Patient
events.summary: 'And Ismail and Idris and Dhul-Kifl — all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.' The Qur'an gathers Idris with two other prophets under a single praise: patience, mercy received, and righteousness.
events.why: Idris is remembered not only for truth and rank but for ṣabr — steadfast patience — the quality the Qur'an ties directly to being admitted into Allah's mercy and counted among the righteous.

paths.title: The Arc of Idris
paths.blurb: All the Qur'an tells of Idris, in order — the man of truth and prophet, raised to a high station, and gathered among the patient whom Allah admitted into His mercy.
